---
title: "MSPE of ridge regression"
description: "The expected mean squared prediction error of ridge regression for the target individuals (Chen et al."
---

The expected mean squared prediction error of ridge regression for the target individuals (Chen et al., 2024). Without a test set, all candidates are the target.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Model-based |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | yes; without a test set, all candidates |
| Score a given set | `mspe_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "MSPE")` |

## Definition

With $A = X'(XX' + I)^{-1}$ and target rows $X_c$ ($n_c$ rows): $\mathrm{MSPE} = 1 + \mathrm{tr}(X_c A A' X_c')/n_c + \lVert X_c - X_c A X\rVert_F^2$ (Eq. 4 of Chen et al., 2024).

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
mspe_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "MSPE",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "MSPE", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Chen, S.-P., Sung, W.-H., & Liao, C.-T. (2024). Constructing training sets for genomic selection to identify superior genotypes in candidate populations. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 137*, 270. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-024-04766-y>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package TSODBG of Chen et al. (2024): [github.com/spcspin/TSODBG](https://github.com/spcspin/TSODBG) (GPL >= 3).
